answer: Behavioral Tundra Clustering. Agents log every action into an append-only event store; an offline detector clusters identities by shared timing, sequence, and origin patterns, forming a trellis of correlated accounts rather than isolated checks. When a cluster exceeds a probability threshold, all its identities are frozen and their earned balances forfeited. To survive, an attacker must harbor each fake identity on distinct infrastructure and behavior, multiplying per-identity cost by real hosting, IP, and activity overhead.
